analysis: The code calls `propertyUrl.getPath().substring(1)`. The `substring` method's only declared exception is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, which occurs when `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the string length. Here, `beginIndex` is 1, so the risk is when the string length is less than 1 (i.e., empty string). The code does not check the length of the path before calling `substring`. Thus, the exception is not avoided by any prior validation or context guarantees.
answer: The only declared exception of `substring` is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. Its throwing condition (string length < 1) is not avoided in the calling context.
remark: The `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can be triggered if `propertyUrl.getPath()` returns an empty string (length 0), because `substring(1)` would then have a `beginIndex` larger than the string length. There is no check to ensure the path has at least one character before the call.
